ruledBy: Astra editorial review, adopted as Al's ruling (his instruction, 2026-09-05; veto list: none)
note: KEEP and FIX (fixed wording) are kept. KILL is held as `unruled`, NOT rejected — Al ruled that explicitly, so no downstream step may treat a KILL as struck. New-lines CSV rows are kept with source astra-new. astraTime is Astra's own visual reading of the hour and does not override the photograph's rotation slot.

kept.text: Your alarm has no idea what it's asking.
The slippers are on. The rest is negotiable.

unruled.text: The grass is wet, the air is cold, and the jersey was not optional.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories grass, cold and the visible jersey.

unruled.text: Dew this heavy means the night got properly cold and stayed there.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: explains dew; no human turn.

unruled.text: Small dog, thick jersey, short patrol: winter mornings run on reduced hours.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: dog-and-jersey caption dressed as an opening-hours joke.

kept.text: Cold enough to end the jacket argument.
kept.fixedFrom: That jacket call was made by one look through the kitchen window.

kept.text: That jacket argument is over before breakfast.
School starts soon. Your fingers haven't.

unruled.text: The zip goes all the way up today; the walk to the gate has teeth.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the zip; teeth merely decorate the cold.

unruled.text: Beanie plus puffer plus school tie: the cold front has reached the uniform.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: clothing inventory followed by a weather label.

kept.text: Work didn't get the message about staying in.
Up before the sun. Still not impressed.

unruled.text: You can see his breath, and the sheep are wearing the only good answer.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: breath and sheep supply the entire joke.

unruled.text: The Karoo does its coldest hour right before its prettiest one.
unruled.reason: R2/R4 fail: tourist-board prettiness replaces the reader's day.

unruled.text: The sheep bunched before he opened the gate; they read the cold first.
unruled.reason: R5/R8 fail: sheep caption needlessly outsmarts the working farmer.

kept.text: Frost first. Your plans can wait ten minutes.
kept.fixedFrom: That windscreen is a ten-minute job and the kettle knows its part.

kept.text: The car coughed twice before it agreed to start.
The car would also like another five minutes.
You left early. The windscreen disagreed.

unruled.text: The sky is clear and the car is white, and those two facts are related.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: explains the photograph instead of earning a turn.

kept.text: Cold indoors too. Keep your jacket on.
kept.fixedFrom: Cold that reaches through a window gets met with wool and a full kettle.

kept.text: The dog refused to go outside. Fair.
Do we actually need milk, or just want it?
The spare blanket is now the main blanket.

unruled.text: One look at that white lawn and the blanket vote was unanimous.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: visible lawn and blanket remain the whole mechanism.

kept.text: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.
You've bought that coffee mostly for your hands.
Have a sip. Your fingers can take a turn.

unruled.text: Coffee outside in this is a commitment, and she has made it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates her coffee outing rather than addressing yours.

unruled.text: Gloves-around-the-cup weather: the coffee is doing two jobs at once.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: labels the visible grip with a cumbersome compound.

kept.text: Tonight's plans fit under one duvet.
Supper had better be hot. This is not a request.

unruled.text: The mist has moved into the valley for the night and locked the gate behind it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: mist and gate gain personalities, not a human consequence.

unruled.text: The valley pulled its blanket up early; the hills stay out a bit later.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: decorative landscape poetry.

unruled.text: That mist is tomorrow morning's frost out doing a site inspection.
unruled.reason: R1/R4 fail: invented frost forecast; bureaucracy replaces ordinary life.

kept.text: Cold again. The car heater means well.
kept.fixedFrom: Berg air gets in through the vents no matter what the heater says.

kept.text: Your toes get the car heater before your face.
Dinner can wait. Feeling your feet comes first.

unruled.text: Snow on the high ground, headlights on early: the pass has gone winter.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: snow, headlights, pass; a complete picture inventory.

unruled.text: The sun is leaving the mountains one shelf at a time.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: scenic caption without a joke.

kept.text: The heater went on at four and the cat clocked in at one minute past.
The heater is your best friend. Your only friend.
Choose your seat before the cat gets ideas.
You're getting up? Bring tea while you're brave.

unruled.text: It is heater season, and the best seat in the house has fur on it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: identifies the heater and its visible furry occupant.

kept.text: The dishes can soak a little longer.
One more log. That was the last one three logs ago.

unruled.text: That door is open to a properly cold night, and nobody in here minds.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: open-door caption with an unsupported reaction.

unruled.text: Outside is for the stars tonight; everything with fur voted fireplace.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: dresses the visible dog-and-fire arrangement as a vote.

unruled.text: The mug is steaming, the logs are in, and winter can do its worst.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: cosy stock-photo copy inventories props.

kept.text: Home has suddenly become your favourite venue.
A table outside? We'll take the bill.

unruled.text: The cold cleared the whole street an hour before closing time.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the empty street; invented timing adds little.

unruled.text: Every streetlamp down the road is lighting nobody; winter nights empty a dorp early.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the empty street and its lamps.

unruled.text: One warm window holding out against a street that has given up.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: moody window caption, no reader or turn.

kept.text: Bedtime finally has somebody on its side.
One more chapter. Nobody said get out of bed.

unruled.text: Beanie, snood, torch, book: winter nights build the best reading rooms.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: prop inventory becomes a lifestyle endorsement.

unruled.text: Only the eyes are getting any cold tonight, and they are busy.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: clothing caption; visible hands also contradict 'only'.

unruled.text: A night this cold turns a wooden hok into a library.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: names the setting; strained library metaphor adds little.

kept.text: Getting dressed feels like taking a layer off.
You miss your bed. You're still in the house.

unruled.text: The warmest place in the province was abandoned here at about six-fifteen.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: abandoned-bed caption inflated by invented time and geography.

unruled.text: The window says mist and bare branches; the bed rests its case.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly narrates window, branches and bed.

unruled.text: The duvet understood the assignment.
unruled.reason: R7 fail: borrowed internet catchphrase, interchangeable with any successful object.

kept.text: The first ten minutes of this Sunday belong to a credit card and the demister.
Your car has asked to work from home.
Ten minutes early. Spent all ten on the windscreen.

unruled.text: Minus something this morning: the windscreen has grown its own art collection.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes the windscreen pattern as art.

unruled.text: Frost on the grass, ferns on the glass — the night went well below zero here.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: frost description and rhyme substitute for a joke.

kept.text: The duvet's coming too. It has earned the outing.
A jersey over pyjamas counts as getting dressed.

unruled.text: Construction finished at nine: one duvet cave, single occupant, no visitors till spring.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the duvet cave through a property-listing routine.

unruled.text: The day outside never got light properly, so the day inside went underground.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: vague metaphor retells the indoor retreat.

unruled.text: Blanket burrito mode: activated.
unruled.reason: R7 fail: imported food metaphor plus stock 'mode activated' template.

kept.text: Cold like this makes a walk feel like work.
kept.fixedFrom: Cold like this turns the morning walk into an errand.

kept.text: Even the short way home feels ambitious.
Dry socks first. We can talk while you find them.

unruled.text: Both of them are dressed for this, and neither is pretending to enjoy it.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates clothing and assigns the pictured pair feelings.

unruled.text: Wet road, grey sky, dog in a jersey: winter is fully operational.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: literal road, sky and jersey inventory.

kept.text: We can disagree under the same blanket.
Move closer. Nobody's asking you to forgive anyone.

unruled.text: One patch of sun came into this lounge and the dog got there first.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the dog occupying the visible sun patch.

unruled.text: Four people share the blanket; the dog negotiated a private sunbeam.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: restates the complete visual joke.

unruled.text: Winter maths: one blanket, four opinions, and a dog holding the only warm square.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: counts the props and overexplains the contrast.

kept.text: Your fingers have declined the early start.
Ready to leave. Your car would like a word.

unruled.text: The morning's second kettle has nothing to do with tea.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: neat understatement still captions the pictured kettle's use.

unruled.text: Frost thick enough that the Polo gets a hot drink before he does.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: car-drinking metaphor narrates the visible pour.

unruled.text: Steam over the windscreen at seven means the night dipped properly below freezing.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: explains steam and invents an exact hour.

kept.text: Cold evening. Even the rain is hesitating.
kept.fixedFrom: That sky has been threatening since lunch and the stoep called its bluff.

kept.text: Salad has been postponed until further notice.
Supper's ready. The camera can eat later.

unruled.text: The mug is out, the shoes are off, and the cold is being watched from cover.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories the mug, shoes and shelter.

unruled.text: Steam off the coffee, cold on the air — the stoep is exactly between them.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: coffee-and-stoep mood caption.

kept.text: The scenic route can manage without you.
You've had fresh air. Nobody said how much.

unruled.text: The mountain is in there somewhere, wrapped up for the winter.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes the obscured mountain using a blanket metaphor.

unruled.text: The beach has gone to one colour, and it is the cold one.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes the photograph's colour.

unruled.text: Nobody's footprints on that sand today; the cold is keeping its beach to itself.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: absence of footprints becomes a beach caption.

kept.text: Cold tonight. Hot chocolate counts as kit.
kept.fixedFrom: Hot chocolate has been promoted to equipment tonight, and the view earned it.

kept.text: Make mine something I have to blow on.
Another round. With handles this time.

unruled.text: Cape Town got Alps for one evening and the whole city is out on balconies.
unruled.reason: R2/R7 fail: tourism slogan, location lock and invented citywide behaviour.

unruled.text: The mountain wears white maybe twice a winter, and tonight is one of them.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: scenic description with an unsupported frequency claim.

kept.text: The bins will still be there in the morning.
You wore pyjamas out. An ambitious little outfit.

unruled.text: His breath is making better clouds than the sky managed all day.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: breath-versus-sky comparison narrates the photograph.

unruled.text: Clear night, wet steps, visible breath: the frost is filling in its paperwork.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: picture inventory followed by decorative paperwork.

unruled.text: One last look at a sky that is about to get seriously cold.
unruled.reason: R3/R4 fail: ominous sky caption without an everyday payoff.

kept.text: The house has one warm room after dark, and it is wherever the blanket is.
My hot water bottle is staying over.
kept.fixedFrom: Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.

kept.text: Even the kettle is putting in overtime.
Deadline tonight. Fingers still negotiating.

unruled.text: Fingerless gloves at a laptop: winter has entered the home office.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: names the visible gloves and laptop, then labels winter.

kept.text: Romance is remembering the spare warm socks.
One blanket for two? Let's stay married.

unruled.text: A Karoo night trades warmth for stars, and they took the deal.
unruled.reason: R2/R7 fail: destination advertising masquerades as a weather bargain.

unruled.text: The fire handles the front; the blanket handles the back; the sky handles everything else.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: prop inventory ends in vague scenic uplift.

unruled.text: Cold enough to share one blanket, clear enough to make it worth it.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: stock camping caption sells the visible arrangement.

kept.text: Matching socks have slipped down the list.
Two pairs on. Suddenly the shoes are the problem.

unruled.text: Socks go on the heater first; feet join later — the winter system works.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates the heater-and-socks setup as household instructions.

unruled.text: The heater has one job this morning and it is these socks.
unruled.reason: R5/R6 fail: labels visible socks and invents morning.

unruled.text: Outside is white at the edges; inside, wool is being pre-heated.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: describes frost and warming wool.

kept.text: Cold and wet. One complaint wasn't enough.
kept.fixedFrom: Beanie-and-brolly weather: the cold and the wet are double-teaming today.

kept.text: Complaining is allowed from under the blanket.
Our demands are modest. Dry socks and feeling toes.

unruled.text: The road gave up before they did, which is the whole story of a Cape winter.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: captions road closure and adds regional shorthand.

unruled.text: The sign says the rain won; the faces say it didn't.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: tells us what the sign and faces show.

kept.text: Your summer clothes can stop volunteering.
You dressed for yesterday. Yesterday apologises.

unruled.text: Somebody's optimism is still on the table, under a millimetre of frost.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: sunglasses become 'optimism', but the joke stays on-table.

unruled.text: Those were left out when this was still a sunglasses kind of place.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains why the pictured sunglasses were left outside.

unruled.text: Grey sky, white table: the patio has switched seasons without asking anyone.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: sky-and-table colour inventory.

kept.text: You need that jersey more than it needs washing.
The second layer stays. Yes, even in the sun.

unruled.text: Snow on the berg, washing on the line: cold enough to freeze, dry enough to try.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: captions snow and washing, then adds rhyme.

unruled.text: Even the washing is all jerseys today, and the mountains explain why.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly makes the mountains explain the washing.

unruled.text: The sun is doing the drying and the snow is doing the reminding.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: assigns jobs to visible sun and snow.

kept.text: Fire first. Then we can discuss breakfast.
kept.fixedFrom: The chimney got lit before the kettle did, and both were the right call.

kept.text: Anyone still insisting on iced coffee?
Breakfast can wait. Feeling your hands can't.

unruled.text: Smoke going straight up means cold, still and not one breath of wind.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: smoke explanation, no ordinary-life turn.

unruled.text: Frost on the wall, steam on the mugs: the morning is minus-something and perfect.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: scenic inventory ends in tourist-board approval.

kept.text: It's jersey weather. Under your jersey.
kept.fixedFrom: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.

kept.text: A nod will do; your hands are staying in your pockets.
Back for the scarf. You were nearly brave.

unruled.text: The jersey got promoted to balaclava somewhere between the door and the gate.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: promotion metaphor describes the visible pulled-up jersey.

unruled.text: The air found the one gap in the outfit and he is closing it by hand.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: narrates his visible hands and clothing.

kept.text: You're making tea? Suddenly everyone needs some.
The blanket comes too. It's only the kitchen.

unruled.text: Chair turned to the heater, blanket up, tea close: winter Sunday, executed correctly.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: chair, blanket and tea inventory with a congratulatory label.

unruled.text: Every bar of that heater is on, which is all the weather report you need.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explicitly substitutes the pictured heater for the forecast.

unruled.text: Cold enough that the armchair migrated toward the plug points.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: migration metaphor describes the pictured chair's position.

kept.text: The weeds can enjoy another day of freedom.
Gardening can stay a plan. A very good plan.

unruled.text: The garden tap grew a white beard overnight; the night was that serious.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: frost on the tap becomes a visual beard.

unruled.text: That drop has been thinking about letting go since about four this morning.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: anthropomorphises the pictured drop without leaving it.

unruled.text: Frost right down to the washers — last night went properly below zero.
unruled.reason: R3/R5 fail: explains frost instead of making a joke.

kept.text: Even the boerboel checked the weather and sat back down.
The walk is still being discussed by both parties.
You said outside. The dog heard something else.

unruled.text: The yard is wet, the air is cold, and security has suspended patrols.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: yard-and-dog caption behind a security metaphor.

unruled.text: That is not a dog refusing a walk; that is a dog reading a forecast.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: laboriously tells the reader how to interpret the dog.

kept.text: Rain's stopped. There goes one excuse.
kept.fixedFrom: The cold front left an hour ago and took the excuses with it.

kept.text: You can keep complaining on the walk home.
One excuse gone. You still have several.

unruled.text: Wet bricks doubling the sunset: the storm's apology, accepted by everybody out here.
unruled.reason: R2/R5 fail: sunset caption adds universal approval.

unruled.text: Beanies plus sunset means the rain has moved on and the cold stayed.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: explains the beanies and sunset.

kept.text: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
Everyone suddenly wants a turn at the braai.
The meat is done. Nobody's putting the fire out.

unruled.text: Frost on the lawn and wors on the grid: a Cape winter compromise.
unruled.reason: R5/R7 fail: frost-and-wors inventory tied to the Cape.

unruled.text: Beanies on, fire lit, wine poured: the cold is now someone else's problem.
unruled.reason: R5 fail: inventories clothes, fire and wine before a stock payoff.
